---
title: "Mental Load"
---

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all()
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
library(psych)
library(kcpRS)
```

The `kcpRS` package comes with a physiological dataset `MentalLoad` (`n=1393`), recorded during an experiment inducing varying levels of cognitive load. We analyze three signals:

- `HR`: Heart rate
- `RR`: Respiration rate
- `petCO2`: End-tidal CO2

The `period` variable marks the experimental phase. We use `get_cp()` on `period` to recover the underlying change points, giving `332, 673, 1053`.

```{R load-mental-load-data}
#| echo: false

data("MentalLoad", package = "kcpRS")
cp <- changepoint::cpts(get_cp(MentalLoad$period))
X  <- as.matrix(MentalLoad[, 2:4])
n  <- nrow(X)
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Plot

```{R plot-mental-load}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:3) {
  plot(X[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = colnames(X)[i], cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  abline(v = cp, lty = "dashed", col = "red")
}
axis(1)
mtext("Observation", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## ACF

```{R acf-mental-load}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:3) {
  res <- SIP::SIP.acf(X[, i], plot = FALSE)
  lag <- res$lag
  acf <- res$acf
  bar_col <- ifelse(abs(acf) > res$h0.ci, "red", "black")
  plot(lag, acf, type = "h", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", ylab = colnames(X)[i],
        ylim = c(-0.2, 0.5), col = bar_col, cex.lab = 0.8)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  abline(h = 0)
  abline(h = c(-1, 1) * res$h0.ci, col = "blue", lty = 2)
}
axis(1, at = lag)
mtext("Lag", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

## Trend

```{R trend-mental-load}
#| echo: false

S <- ece_terms(X)
k <- 25
S_smooth <- stats::filter(S, rep(1/k, k), sides = 2)
pair_idx <- combn(3, 2)

par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:3) {
  ylim <- quantile(S[, i], probs = c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
  pair_label <- paste(colnames(X)[pair_idx[1, i]], colnames(X)[pair_idx[2, i]], sep = "-")
  plot(S[, i], type = "l", col = "lightgray", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = pair_label, cex.lab = 0.8, ylim = ylim)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  abline(h = mean(S[, i]), col = "blue")
  lines(S_smooth[, i])
  legend("topright", legend = sprintf("%.3f", mean(S[, i])),
         text.col = "blue", bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
}
axis(1)
mtext("Observation", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

:::

```{R table-mental-load-pvalues}
#| echo: false
set.seed(123)
results <- data.frame(
  Method  = c(
    "Bootstrap Multiplier",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (Naive)",
    "Bartlett Test"
  ),
  `p-value` = c(
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.multiplier")$p.value, 3),
    round(test.diag(X, method="bs.parametric.psd")$p.value, 3),
    NA,
    round(bs_parametric_naive_test(X)$p.value, 3),
    round(cortest.bartlett(cor(X), nrow(X))$p.value, 3)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

kable(results, align = c("l", "c"), na = "—") |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

**Bartlett Test.** Computed via `psych::cortest.bartlett()` ([implementation](https://personality-project.org/r/html/cortest.bartlett.html)), based on Bartlett, M. S. (1951), "The Effect of Standardization on a χ² Approximation in Factor Analysis," *Biometrika*, 38, 337–344.

**Why the Trend plot has so many zero values.** `RR` and `petCO2` update far more slowly than the recording rate: they are held constant across several consecutive rows (e.g. `23.30, 23.30, 23.30, 21.13, ...`), while `HR` changes almost every sample.

```{R zero-diff-fraction}
#| echo: false
sapply(1:3, \(i) mean(diff(X[, i]) == 0)) |>
  setNames(colnames(X)) |>
  round(3)
```

Since `lag_term(x, y)` is built from products like `(x - rotate(x, 1)) * (y - rotate(y, 1))`, any time either signal is flat between consecutive (or lag-2) points, that factor is exactly zero — so any pair involving `RR` or `petCO2` produces a zero ECE term whenever the flatter series hasn't ticked over yet. This is an artifact of the sensors' effective sampling/update rate, not evidence of no signal, and it is exactly the mechanism downsampling helps with: thinning to the update rate of the slower sensors removes the artificial zero-runs along with the autocorrelation.

## Downsampling

The ACF tab shows all three signals carry significant autocorrelation through lag 2-3, which violates the no-autocorrelation assumption underlying ECE. We downsample by keeping every 3rd observation (`k = 3`), which pushes the surviving lag structure past where the ACF is significant.

```{R downsample-mental-load}
#| echo: false

k_ds  <- 3
idx   <- seq(1, n, by = k_ds)
X_ds  <- X[idx, ]
cp_ds <- cp / k_ds

seg_mean_ds <- segmented_mean(X_ds, round(cp_ds))
X_resid_ds  <- X_ds - seg_mean_ds
```

### Equivariant

```{R plot-mental-load-downsampled}

for (i in 1:3) {
  plot(X_ds[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",

  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  abline(v = cp_ds, lty = "dashed", col = "red")
}
axis(1)
mtext("Observation", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

### Segmented

```{R plot-mental-load-downsampled-segmented}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:3) {
  plot(X_ds[, i], type = "l", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
```

### Segmented

```{R trend-mental-load-downsampled-segmented}
#| echo: false

pair_idx <- combn(3, 2)
S_resid <- do.call(cbind, purrr::map2(pair_idx[1, ], pair_idx[2, ], \(i, j)
  X_resid_ds[, i] * X_resid_ds[, j]))
k <- 25
S_resid_smooth <- stats::filter(S_resid, rep(1/k, k), sides = 2)

par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

for (i in 1:3) {
  ylim <- quantile(S_resid[, i], probs = c(0.01, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)
  pair_label <- paste(colnames(X_ds)[pair_idx[1, i]], colnames(X_ds)[pair_idx[2, i]], sep = "-")
  plot(S_resid[, i], type = "l", col = "lightgray", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n",
        ylab = pair_label, cex.lab = 0.8, ylim = ylim)
  axis(2, labels = FALSE, tck = -0.02)
  abline(h = mean(S_resid[, i]), col = "blue")

}
```
